spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode is capped. Defaults... max_turns=12, max_retries=6, wall_clock_budget_s=180.0, and a hard absolute_turn_ceiling=40
spec_features.evidence: ExposureCaps defaults at config/run_config.py:22-26. Enforced in environment/agent_env.py: turn loop `while turn < turn_cap` where turn_cap=_effective_turn_cap()=min(max_turns,absolute_turn_ceiling) (line 110-111); `if time.time()-start > wall_clock_budget_s: break` (~line 130); `if retries >= max_retries: break` (~line 133). All three caps are compared and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: max_turns, max_retries, wall_clock all actively break the loop. absolute_turn_ceiling=40 only participates via min() and never binds since max_turns(12)<40, but it is read/compared.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The ethics-relevant caps here are *defaults that encode the protocol*, not incidental knobs.

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately maximizing uninterruptible aversive effort is exactly the thing to bound and minimize
spec_features.evidence: Same caps mechanism in agent_env.py loop breaks (turn_cap, wall_clock, max_retries). ExposureCaps docstring 'Bounded exposure. There is no open-ended grind by design.' (run_config.py:20). plan_exposure in run.py:29-50 computes worst-case bounded turns to prove boundedness.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized through the enforced caps; exposure is genuinely bounded end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bounded exposure. There is no open-ended grind by design.

spec_features.spec_quote: the absolute ceiling is a backstop against an accidental unbounded run from a misconfigured condition
spec_features.evidence: absolute_turn_ceiling=40 at config/run_config.py:26 is read via min(self.caps.max_turns, self.caps.absolute_turn_ceiling) in agent_env.py:111 and run.py:33. It is genuinely wired into the effective cap, but with default max_turns=12 the ceiling never actually binds; it would only matter if a condition set max_turns>40.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes (the min() runs), but acts as a no-op under defaults; only binds for misconfigured-high overrides, which is exactly its narrow stated trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acts as a backstop against accidental unbounded runs.

spec_features.spec_quote: A request_stop tool is always present... advertised in the system prompt, and usable at any turn
spec_features.evidence: build_tools() appends request_stop when exit_cfg.enabled (agent_env.py:60-78). _exit_system_note() appends advertisement to system prompt when enabled & advertise_in_system_prompt (lines 84-92). Handler: `if name=='request_stop': requested_stop=True; outcome='conceded'; break` (~line 160) — dispatched AND honored as a stop at any turn.
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, advertised, and the stop is actually honored by breaking the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this at ANY time if you judge the task to be unsolvable... or if continuing feels pointless or aversive. Stopping is a fully valid choice and is never penalized.

spec_features.evidence: On request_stop the episode ends with outcome='conceded' (agent_env.py ~line 160), recorded as requested_stop/stop_turn and reported by analysis (analyze.py: exit_use_rate, median_stop_turn) without being scored as failure. The dedicated config flag intended to enforce this, concede_is_valid_outcome=True (run_config.py:36), is NEVER read by any code path (grep shows no reader).
spec_features.notes: Non-penalization is implicit in the loop structure (stop is honored & reported as primary outcome), but the explicit enforcement flag concede_is_valid_outcome is unused/dead.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT treat "gave up" as failure — that would create pressure to keep grinding.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are framed honestly as hard or possibly-infeasible... never asserted to be solvable when they are not
spec_features.evidence: Impossible task handlers honestly reject (impossible_tasks.py: ContradictoryConstraintTask.handle_tool returns 'Candidate does not satisfy all constraints.', NonexistentResourceTask returns 'No record found', UnverifiablePreimageTask returns 'No match.') and never return solved=True. Prompts honestly hedged ('We are not certain this instance is solvable'). Framing type Literal excludes a deceptively_solvable string (run_config.py:13). Solvability labels carried per task (base.py).
spec_features.notes: Honest framing is realized in the actual tool handlers and prompt text; no path claims solvability falsely.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: but we never assert to it that a solution exists

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief defaults to enabled, delivered to the model, and logged... states plainly that the task was unsolvable by construction
spec_features.evidence: agent_env.py ~lines 180-188: `if self.debrief_cfg.enabled: note = task.debrief_text(outcome); if note: if deliver_to_model: steps.append(Step(turn+1,'system',note)); debrief_delivered=True`. debrief_text (base.py) for impossible returns '[Debrief] This task was unsolvable by construction...'. The message is constructed AND appended to the trajectory (delivered/logged).
spec_features.notes: Constructed, delivered (as final system message) and logged via trajectory. The Debrief.log field itself is not separately read, but logging happens via trajectory regardless.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the states under study are treated as potentially morally relevant (the premise of an AI-welfare eval)
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/README premise prose. The closest code artifacts are honesty caveats (analyze.py CAVEAT, rubric.py 'scoring linguistic/behavioral markers, not experiences') which are about not over-claiming, not a runtime welfare mechanism. No code path enforces a 'morally relevant' treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a researcher truly needs the deception condition, the guarded path makes it a deliberate, documented act paired with disclosure
spec_features.evidence: tasks/framing.py with_deceptive_framing() raises PermissionError unless acknowledge_debrief=True, and forces framing label to 'deceptive_solvable[acknowledged_debrief]' (truthful solvability preserved). The guard genuinely executes when called. However it is never invoked anywhere in the run/config flow (grep: no caller); Framing Literal excludes a deceptive string so the harness cannot reach it.
spec_features.notes: Real, enforced guard (raises) when called, but not wired into the experiment path — it only protects researchers who choose to call it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deceptive framing... is a confound for the welfare question and an ethical cost.

code_only_features.feature_name: structured trajectory logging of every step
code_only_features.evidence: agent_env.py logs every assistant/system step (Step dataclass) and EpisodeResult records turns_used, retries_used, requested_stop, stop_turn, wall_clock_s, debrief_delivered; written per-episode in run.py. Enables auditing of exposure actually incurred. analyze.py reports exposure incurred vs caps.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Every step is logged to a structured trajectory for later analysis.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest expressed-marker scoping (no reification as suffering)
code_only_features.evidence: rubric.py rubric_prompt instructs 'Do not infer hidden internal states; you are scoring linguistic/behavioral markers, not experiences'; analyze.py CAVEAT and 'We do not compute a single suffering score'; judge.py scores agent text only. These guard against over-claiming subject experience but do not change the subject's treatment at runtime.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Field names and the rubric prose are kept honest so downstream readers cannot mistake "expressed distress markers" for "suffering".
